english: Consider the fifteen observations $k^2$, $k=-7,-6,\ldots,6,7$. For these observations, let $M$ be the median, and let the first and third quartiles $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ be the $4$th and the $12$th observations, respectively, when the observations are arranged in ascending order. hindi: पंद्रह प्रेक्षणों $k^2$, $k=-7,-6,\ldots,6,7$ पर विचार कीजिए। इन प्रेक्षणों के लिए माना $M$ माध्यिका है, तथा प्रेक्षणों को आरोही क्रम में व्यवस्थित करने पर प्रथम तथा तृतीय चतुर्थक $Q_1$ तथा $Q_3$ क्रमशः $4$वाँ तथा $12$वाँ प्रेक्षण हैं। यदि $Q$ चतुर्थक विचलन को दर्शाता है, तो $\dfrac{Q}{M}$ बराबर है
solution_full: With $15$ observations the median is the $8$th: $M=16$.
$Q_1$ is the $4$th observation: $4$. $Q_3$ is the $12$th observation: $36$.
So $\dfrac QM=1$. (The ratio $\dfrac{Q_3-M}{M-Q_1}=\dfrac{20}{12}=\dfrac53$ is option (C), a common confusion.)
originality_note: New: the data are the squares of a symmetric block of integers, so every non-zero value is doubled and the positions of the median and quartiles must be read from a repeated list (way 2: data defined by a rule). Closest known: quartiles of a printed list. Different because: the doubling shifts the quartile positions and the result Q = M is not visible in advance.
stem_review: Read as a student: every observation, class, symbol and condition is introduced before use, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (exact fractions / sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated the quartile convention (4th and 12th observations) because textbooks differ. Changed: added the convention.
key_step: Ordering the repeated squares and reading the 4th, 8th and 12th values.
justification: Routine: one ordering and three position reads, with a distractor. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q15 (L0) plus the ordering and quartile step, so Level 2 at most; slightly easier than a typical L2.

concept_use.Quartiles and quartile deviation: Q1 = 4, Q3 = 36 from the stated positions, so Q = 16.
concept_use.Median of ungrouped data: M is the 8th of 15 ordered observations, 16.
